name: agent
description: Run or reattach an agent in a worktree (tmux)

options.description: Command to run (default: the agent.command setting)
Agent to run: claude or antigravity (agent.antigravityCommand, default agy); --command wins
Run the agent directly in this terminal, without a tmux session
One of several agents of the worktree: its own tmux session (<agent session>-a-<id>; letters, digits, _ and -, up to 32)
[stop] Stop the default session and every --session one (exit 0 when none runs)

helpText:
Actions:
  start [branch]    run the agent in the worktree's tmux session, or reattach to it (default)
  status [branch]   whether the session exists
  stop [branch]     kill the session

[branch] defaults to the current branch; `kunj agent my-branch` starts. Without tmux (or with
--no-tmux) start runs the agent directly in this terminal, and it stops when the terminal closes.

--session <id> runs one more agent in the worktree, in its own tmux session; status, stop and
start then act on that one. status without it reports every agent of the worktree; stop --all
ends them all. stop with --session or --all exits 0 even when nothing ran.

--agent antigravity runs the Antigravity CLI (agy) instead of agent.command. Only Claude Code
reports when it waits for input; another agent shows as running while its session lives.

options.description: [start] Create the branch in the container from origin/<base>
[start] Base for a new branch (default: preferences.defaultBaseBranch, else the repo default)
[start] Use this image instead of the configured one
[start] Rebuild the image and recreate the container (volumes are kept); [blueprint snapshot] snapshot again even when up to date
[start] Neither build nor use the blueprint's snapshot (tools and setup run in the container)
[start] Keep what a failed start created, for debugging
[list] Skip the per-container status exec (faster listing)
[list] Show every repository's containers; [prune] prune every repository in ~/.kunj/repos.json
[remove|prune] Remove even when the container holds unpushed work (prune: and volumes without a container)
[prune] Only list what would be removed (the default without --yes when stdout is not a terminal, or with --json)
[remove] Keep the workspace and home volumes (and the services' volumes); [start --rebuild] keep the volumes of services no longer declared
[open] Open in a new editor window
[forward] Forward every port the container starts listening on (>= 1024, not in container.forward.ignore)
[forward --auto] Run the forwarder in the background; it exits when the container stops
[blueprint init] Write the host copy (~/.kunj/<repo>/blueprint.json) instead of .kunj/blueprint.json
[blueprint init] Accept the inferred blueprint and overwrite an existing file; [prune] remove without asking, also from a script or with --json
[blueprint snapshot] Clone from origin in the container instead of a bundle the host fetched (origin must be public)
[blueprint snapshot|status] Use this blueprint file instead of the resolved one
[shell] Keep the shell in the container's tmux session sh-<id>; [agent|attach] one of several agents, tmux session agent-<id> (letters, digits, _ and -; up to 32)
[shell|agent] End the --session tmux session, or without --session every shell (sh-*) or agent (agent, agent-*) session; exit 0 whether or not one existed or the container runs
Run on this kunj serve remote (kunj remote add; default: container.remote); "local" forces this machine's Docker

helpText:
Actions:
  start [branch]                       create or resume the branch's container
  shell [branch] [--session <id>]      login shell in /workspace (kept in tmux session sh-<id>; --kill ends it)
  exec [branch] -- <cmd...>            run a command in the container
  agent [branch] [-- <args>]           start or reattach the agent's tmux session (--session <id>: agent-<id>; --kill ends it)
  attach [branch]                      reattach to the agent's tmux session (--session <id>: agent-<id>)
  open [branch] [--new-window]         attach the editor (worktree.editorCommand), starting it if stopped
  forward [branch] <port>|<host>:<port>...  forward localhost ports into the container
  forward [branch] <service>:<port>    forward a sidecar service's port (e.g. postgres:5432)
  forward [branch] --auto [--detach]   forward each port the container listens on, as it appears
  mcp [branch]                         bridge the host MCP servers of container.mcp (foreground)
  logs [branch] [service] [--follow]   output of the container, or of one of its services
  list                                 containers of this repository (the default)
  stop [branch]                        stop, keeping the workspace
  remove [branch]                      remove, refusing while work is unpushed
  prune [--all] [--dry-run]            remove containers of branches gone from origin, orphans and old images
  file read [branch] <path>            print a file of /workspace
  file write [branch] <path>           write stdin to a file of /workspace (content on stdin)
  token status                         where a new container's GitHub token comes from (never prints it)
  token setup                          run claude setup-token, check the token and store it for containers
  token check                          whether the Claude Code token for containers works (one claude -p)

Blueprint (how a new container is set up: tools, setup and maintain commands):
  blueprint init [--global] [--yes]    infer one from this checkout and write .kunj/blueprint.json
  blueprint snapshot [--base <ref>]    optional: build the snapshot ahead of time (--rebuild forces it)
  blueprint status                     which blueprint, its hash and snapshot, stale or not
  blueprint remove                     delete this repository's snapshot images

The blueprint is read from .kunj/blueprint.json in this working tree, else
origin/<default branch>:.kunj/blueprint.json, else ~/.kunj/<repo>/blueprint.json. A new
container starts from its snapshot; start builds the snapshot first when there is none or the
blueprint changed (the first start runs setup once), and falls back to running setup in the
container if that fails. --no-snapshot skips the snapshot.

Services (Postgres, Redis, ...) are declared in the blueprint's "services", container.services
or the devcontainer's compose file; each runs next to the branch container on its own network
and is reached by its name (postgres:5432). They are stopped and removed with the container.

agent also starts a background forward --auto for the container (container.forward.auto: false
turns that off). Forwards only ever listen on 127.0.0.1. With container.mcp set (host config,
e.g. {"chrome": {}}), agent also bridges a browser MCP server on this machine into the
container's Claude Code: a fixed set of browser tools, no file paths, downloads refused, and
navigation only to the container's forwarded ports (or container.mcp.chrome.allowOrigins).

Tokens: a new container gets GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN or GITLAB_TOKEN from the host env when
container.env names it. With none set and origin on GitHub, kunj forwards `gh auth token` as
GH_TOKEN (container.useGhToken: false turns that off). The agent can use that token.

[branch] defaults to the current branch. `ct` is short for `container`.

name: hooks
description: Manage hooks: your scripts that run before and after kunj actions (like git hooks)
helpText:
Hooks are your own scripts or commands that kunj runs before and after its actions, like
git hooks, but around kunj commands (create, switch, commit, pr, ...) rather than git itself.

Actions:
  list (default)          Show every hook, what it receives and what is installed for it
  add <hook> [-g] [-f]    Create a starter script for <hook>, ready for you to edit:
                          a commented /bin/sh template listing the hook's arguments and
                          KUNJ_* variables, already executable (chmod +x).
                          Written to this repository's hooks directory:
                            ~/.kunj/kunj/hooks/<hook>
                          or, with -g/--global, the one used by every repository:
                            ~/.kunj/hooks/<hook>
                          An existing script is left alone unless -f/--force is given.
                          For a one-line command, set hooks.<hook> in the config instead.
  run <hook> [target]     Run a hook now, to test it. [target] is a worktree for the worktree
                          hooks and a branch for the others (default: the current one)
  path [-g]               Print the repo (or global) hooks directory

Hooks:
  pre-worktree-create    Runs before `kunj worktree add` creates a worktree. Can abort.
                         args: $1 worktree-path, $2 branch
  post-worktree-create   Runs inside a freshly created worktree, after keep files have been
                         copied in (e.g. to install dependencies).
                         args: $1 worktree-path, $2 branch
  pre-worktree-delete    Runs inside a worktree before `kunj worktree remove` deletes it.
                         Can abort.
                         args: $1 worktree-path, $2 branch
  post-worktree-delete   Runs from the main worktree after a worktree has been removed (e.g.
                         to clean up containers or databases).
                         args: $1 worktree-path, $2 branch
  pre-branch-create      Runs before `kunj create` or `kunj switch -c` creates a branch. Can
                         abort.
                         args: $1 branch, $2 previous-branch
  post-branch-create     Runs after `kunj create` or `kunj switch -c` has created and
                         switched to a branch.
                         args: $1 branch, $2 previous-branch
  pre-branch-switch      Runs before `kunj switch` changes branch. Can abort.
                         args: $1 branch, $2 previous-branch
  post-branch-switch     Runs after `kunj switch` has changed branch and restored its stash
                         (e.g. to install dependencies).
                         args: $1 branch, $2 previous-branch
  pre-branch-delete      Runs before `kunj delete` deletes a branch. Can abort.
                         args: $1 branch
  post-branch-delete     Runs after `kunj delete` has deleted a branch.
                         args: $1 branch
  pre-commit             Runs after `kunj commit` has staged the files, before the message
                         is written. Can abort.
                         args: $1 branch
  commit-msg             Runs with the (AI-generated or typed) message in a file before
                         `kunj commit` commits; it may edit the file. Can abort.
                         args: $1 message-file, $2 branch
  post-commit            Runs after `kunj commit` has created a commit, before pushing.
                         args: $1 branch
  pre-pr-create          Runs before `kunj pr` pushes the branch and opens a pull request.
                         Can abort.
                         args: $1 branch, $2 base-branch, $3 title
  post-pr-create         Runs after `kunj pr` has opened a pull request.
                         args: $1 branch, $2 base-branch, $3 title, $4 pr-url
  pre-stash              Runs before kunj stashes changes (`kunj stash` or the auto-stash on
                         create/switch). Can abort.
                         args: $1 branch, $2 message
  post-stash             Runs after kunj has stashed changes.
                         args: $1 branch, $2 message
  pre-container-create   Runs before `kunj container start` creates a container. Can abort.
                         args: $1 branch, $2 container, $3 image
  post-container-create  Runs after `kunj container start` has created and seeded a
                         container.
                         args: $1 branch, $2 container, $3 image
  pre-container-delete   Runs before `kunj container remove` deletes a container. Can abort.
                         args: $1 branch, $2 container, $3 image
  post-container-delete  Runs after `kunj container remove` has removed a container.
                         args: $1 branch, $2 container, $3 image

Where hooks come from (all of them run, in this order):
  1. ~/.kunj/hooks/<hook>            global, every repository
  2. ~/.kunj/<repo>/hooks/<hook>     this repository only
     Either may also be a directory <hook>.d/ whose scripts run in name order.
     Scripts must be executable (chmod +x); *.sample files and dotfiles are ignored.
  3. The hooks.<hook> config setting: a shell command, or a JSON array of commands

What a hook receives:
  Arguments      as listed above, as $1, $2, ...
  Environment    each argument as KUNJ_<ARG> (KUNJ_BRANCH, KUNJ_PREVIOUS_BRANCH, KUNJ_PR_URL, ...),
                 plus KUNJ_HOOK, KUNJ_REPO_ROOT, KUNJ_REPO_CONFIG and KUNJ_REPO_NAME
  Config vars    config commands can use each argument as a camelCase ${...} variable
                 (${branch}, ${previousBranch}, ${prUrl}, ${worktree}) and ${repoRoot}, ${repoName}, ...
                 Values are quoted for you: ${branch} and "${branch}" both pass them literally.
  Directory      the worktree for post-worktree-create and pre-worktree-delete, the main
                 worktree for the other worktree hooks, otherwise where kunj was run

Exit status:
  A pre-* or commit-msg hook that exits non-zero stops the action and later hooks do not run.
  A post-* hook cannot undo anything; a failure is shown as a warning.
  commit-msg may rewrite the message file ($1); kunj commits whatever the file holds afterwards.
  Pass --no-hooks to create, switch, delete, commit, pr, stash or worktree to skip hooks once.
  With --json, hook output goes to stderr so the JSON on stdout stays clean.

Examples:
  kunj hooks                                   list hooks and what is installed
  kunj hooks add post-branch-switch            scaffold ~/.kunj/<repo>/hooks/post-branch-switch
  kunj hooks add pre-commit -g                 scaffold a global pre-commit hook
  kunj hooks run commit-msg                    try commit-msg against a sample message
  kunj config --set hooks.post-worktree-create="npm install"
  kunj config --set hooks.pre-pr-create="npm run lint && npm test"
  kunj commit --no-hooks                       commit without running kunj hooks

options.description: [add] Reach the server through an SSH tunnel to user@host (the server listens on its loopback)
[add] The server's port on the box, with --ssh (default 7433)

[add] Accept an http:// URL to a non-loopback address: the token, secrets and terminals travel unencrypted, so only on a network that already encrypts (Tailscale, WireGuard) or that you trust

helpText:
Actions:
  add <name> --ssh user@host [--port n]   a server reached through an SSH tunnel kunj opens
  add <name> --url https://…             a server you put behind TLS yourself
  add <name> --url http://… --allow-insecure-http
                                         plain http over a network that already encrypts (a tailnet)
  list (default)                         the known remotes, without their tokens
  remove <name>
  ping <name>                            versions, features and Docker context of the server
  token <name>                           replace the stored token

Then kunj ct … --remote <name>, or kunj config --set container.remote=<name> in the repository,
runs that repository's containers there. --remote local forces this machine's Docker.
Remotes are kept in ~/.kunj/remotes.json (0600).

name: run
description: Run a command with the host secrets in its environment

options.description: Resolve the secrets of this branch (default: the current one)
On an error before the command starts, wait for Enter (tmux panes close with the process)

helpText:
Put -- before the command so its own options are not read as kunj's:
  kunj run -- npm run dev
  kunj run --branch feature/x -- $SHELL -l

The command gets the global, repo and branch secrets whose targets include host and that are
delivered as environment variables. File deliveries are written into this worktree first (a file
git does not ignore is skipped with a warning). The exit code is the command's.

name: secret
description: Manage encrypted secrets and where they are delivered

options.description: Branch scope (without a name: the current branch)
[set, import] host, container or host,container (default both)
[set, import] Also render into this file, relative to the worktree (import: default .env)
[set, import] Do not deliver as an environment variable
[import] Delete the source file (and its keep copy) afterwards
[apply] Write files that git does not ignore

helpText:
Actions:
  set NAME           store a value (hidden prompt, or stdin when piped; never an argument)
  import <file>      import a .env file (default: repo scope, host and container, env plus .env)
  list               names, scope, targets and delivery; never values
  get NAME           print one value (refused with --json)
  rm NAME            remove one (of the scope given by --global / --branch)
  env                resolved secrets as export lines, for eval (refused with --json)
  apply [-a]         render file deliveries into this worktree (or every one)

Secrets are stored at repo scope unless --global or --branch is given. Reads (get, env, apply)
resolve global, then repo, then the branch (the current one unless --branch names another).

name: serve
description: Serve this machine's Docker to kunj on other machines (remote containers)

options.description: Address to listen on (default 127.0.0.1:7433); a non-loopback address needs --allow-remote-listen
Listen on a non-loopback address (plain HTTP on your network: prefer an SSH tunnel or a TLS proxy)
Let clients use these --runtime values, e.g. sysbox-runc (comma-separated or repeated)
Log every request (method, route, status, duration); refusals are always logged
[token] Replace the token; every client must be given the new one

helpText:
Actions:
  (default)        run the server until Ctrl-C; prints the token the first time
  token            print the token (kunj remote add <name> … needs it on the laptop)

The server listens on this machine's loopback. From the laptop, reach it through an SSH tunnel kunj
opens (kunj remote add box --ssh user@box) or a URL you have put behind TLS (--url https://…).
Anyone with the token controls the containers kunj makes here, so keep it like an SSH key.
The token is in ~/.kunj/serve/token (0600).
